claim: Local real estate assessors must assess at 100 percent fair market value in localities with annual assessments.
Local board of equalization hears complaints and may increase or decrease assessments; assessor's valuation is presumed correct.
On appeal to the board, taxpayer must show by a preponderance of the evidence that property is valued above fair market value or not uniformly assessed.
Market sales through December 31 before the assessment's effective date may be considered if submitted by the locality's application deadline.

Application to the commissioner of the revenue for correction: within three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from assessment date, whichever is later; real estate corrections limited to errors by the commissioner or factual errors in reassessment.
Relief may be sought in circuit court within three years of the last day of the tax year, or one year from assessment or final determination, whichever is later.
In circuit court proceedings, the taxpayer burden of proof applies except in proceedings seeking relief from real property taxes.

Localities may by ordinance exempt or defer real estate taxes for owner-occupied sole dwellings of persons at least 65 or, if the ordinance provides, permanently and totally disabled.
Real property of a veteran rated 100 percent service-connected, permanent and total disabled, occupied as principal residence, is exempt from real property tax (tax years from 2011).
Surviving spouse of an eligible veteran qualifies so long as the spouse does not remarry.
Creditor-process homestead exemption: $5,000 ($10,000 if age 65+), plus up to $50,000 in value for principal residence of householder or dependents, plus $500 per dependent.

State recordation tax on deeds: 25 cents per $100 of the greater of consideration or actual value.
Additional grantor tax: 50 cents per $500 of consideration (value over $100), excluding liens remaining on the property.
Grantor tax is paid by the grantor, but grantor and grantee may arrange for the grantee to pay all or part.
Deed cannot be recorded unless consideration is stated on the first page and the clerk certifies the tax was paid.
Cities and counties may impose a local recordation tax equal to one-third of the state recordation tax.
Exemptions include deeds pursuant to divorce decree, partition deeds, and transfers to a revocable trust where grantors and beneficiaries are the same and no consideration passes.
No recordation tax on a deed of gift, quitclaim deed, or TOD deed when no consideration passes, or a deed of distribution; deed must so state.
UNCONFIRMED: Virginia has no separate documentary 'transfer tax' name; recordation taxes serve that role (statement not found verbatim on an official page).
Virginia foreclosure is typically non-judicial: on default the trustee may declare the debt due and sell at auction under the deed of trust.
Secured party may appoint a substitute trustee by recorded instrument.
Written notice of sale must be mailed to the owner by certified or registered mail at least 60 days before sale for owner-occupied residential property (14 days for other deeds of trust).
Notice for owner-occupied residential must state 'This is NOT a notice to vacate the premises' and list HUD counseling and legal aid contacts.
If no publication count is stated, trustee advertises once a week for four successive weeks (five days in or next to a city); sale held 8 to 30 days after advertising.
Defective advertisement makes the sale voidable by the court on petition.
Sale proceeds go to trustee expenses, then priority taxes, then secured debts and inferior liens, with the residue paid to the grantor.

A money judgment is a lien on real estate from the time it is recorded on the clerk's judgment lien docket.
Enforcement of a judgment lien is in equity; the court may decree sale if rents and profits will not satisfy the judgment in five years.
No bill to enforce a judgment lien is entertained if real estate is the debtor's primary residence and the judgment is $25,000 or less excluding interest and costs (association assessments: $5,000).
